meta.status: final for Space Apps 2026 submission; place names are automatic (GeoNames reverse geocoding) - verify before publishing
meta.score_formula: task score = 100 * exp( sum(w * ln(max(s, eps))) / sum(w) ), eps = 0.01, w = 1 for every feature (equal-weight geometric mean). Every listed feature is required: a cell missing any feature is not scored.
meta.score_formula_note: Not the lunar weighted arithmetic mean 100*sum(w*c*s)/sum(w*c): one feature near 0 pulls the Mars score toward 0 (a site that fails one requirement cannot be compensated by others). c = 1 everywhere.
meta.total_score_optional: weighted geometric mean of the scored tests with weight_roc renormalised over the tests the user selects; reference only
meta.profile_formula: dimension = equal-weight geometric mean of its variable similarities (floor 0.01); overall = equal-weight geometric mean of the 5 scored dimensions x 100; ranked cells need >= 80% of dimensions and >= 80% of variables with data
meta.classification_rule: s >= 0.6 similar; s < 0.3 different; otherwise partial
meta.known_analog_rule: a candidate within 50 km of a known analog site (data/labels/known_analogs.csv) is flagged and listed under known_analogs_in_top instead of new_candidates
meta.ice_rule: tests with applies = ice (R3, R5) are scored only for Mars targets with SWIM Ci >= 0.1

ranking_groups.new_candidates: top 10 Earth sites for this test and Mars site, known analogs removed, >= 150 km apart
ranking_groups.known_analogs_in_top: known analog sites that made the top 20 (shown for credibility)
ranking_groups.known_analogs_validation: every known analog site with its score and global top-% for this test
ranking_groups.least_similar: 3 lowest-scoring fully observed sites (contrast); present only after --grid

meta.ai_disclosure: Scoring code, data-processing scripts and this export were written with Claude (Anthropic); the team chose the method, reviewed the code and checked the results.
limitations: R2 (visual navigation) is not evaluated: no global image-texture data.
Earth cells are 0.1 degree (~11 km); Mars study circles have radii of 25-50 km. Sub-cell terrain is unresolved.
Earth slope is the 230 m GMTED2010 median per cell, not the 100 m scale in the landing requirement.
Lithology is a coarse class match (GLiM 0.5 degree vs USGS SIM 3292).
Temperature and aridity are scored as 'more extreme is closer' (Earth cannot reach Mars values), so they do not change between Mars targets.
Seven Mars targets; biology and subsurface dimensions are not scored.
meta.site_limit_note: Mars study circles have radii of 25 or 50 km, as recorded for each site.

mars_sites.name: Jezero Crater
mars_sites.source: Teammate's targets.yaml (rounded centre of the Jezero area). A 25 km circle contains the Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing, 18.4447 N 77.4508 E): https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/images/pia24483-welcome-to-octavia-e-butler-landing/

mars_sites.name: Gale Crater
mars_sites.source: Teammate's targets.yaml (Gale crater centre). Note: Curiosity's Bradbury Landing (4.5895 S 137.4417 E) is about 48 km away, outside the 25 km circle, so the circle covers the crater floor and the foot of Mount Sharp, not the landing site.

mars_sites.name: Arcadia Planitia (shallow ground ice)
mars_sites.source: Teammate's targets.yaml. Inside the SWIM Arcadia study region (150-225 E, 0-60 N); SWIM ice consistency about 0.5 here. Morgan et al. 2021, Nature Astronomy 5:230; https://swim.psi.edu/resources/abstracts/LPSC2019/2069.pdf

mars_sites.name: Oxia Planum (ExoMars Rosalind Franklin landing site)
mars_sites.source: ESA: Oxia Planum site 18.20N 335.45E; landing ellipse 104 x 19 km, clay-bearing Noachian plains. https://exploration.esa.int/mars/54724-oxia-planum/

mars_sites.name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity landing site, Eagle crater)
mars_sites.source: NASA/JPL: Eagle crater 1.95S 354.47E, Opportunity landing site (hematite spherules, sulfate-rich sandstones). https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/images/rovers-landing-hardware-at-eagle-crater-mars
